queries: In Arabidopsis thaliana, DNA methylation is established and maintained at three sequence contexts—CG, CHG, and CHH—through distinct enzymatic pathways. Maintenance of CG methylation is primarily carried out by METHYLTRANSFERASE 1 (MET1), which recognizes hemimethylated CG sites during DNA replication and restores symmetric methylation on the daughter strand. For CHG methylation, the plant-specific CHROMOMETHYLASE 3 (CMT3) is the key maintenance enzyme, acting in concert with the histone H3K9 methyltransferase KYP/SUVH4 to reinforce methylation at these symmetric sites. CHH methylation, being asymmetric, cannot be maintained by a replication-coupled mechanism; instead, it relies on continuous de novo methylation by DOMAINS REARRANGED METHYLTRANSFERASE 2 (DRM2), which is guided by the RNA-directed DNA methylation (RdDM) pathway. In the canonical RdDM pathway, plant-specific RNA polymerase IV (Pol IV) produces single-stranded RNAs that are converted into double-stranded RNAs by RNA-DEPENDENT RNA POLYMERASE 2 (RDR2). These dsRNAs are then processed by DICER-LIKE 3 (DCL3) into 24-nucleotide small interfering RNAs (siRNAs). The siRNAs are loaded into ARGONAUTE 4 (AGO4), which guides the AGO4-siRNA complex to complementary nascent scaffold transcripts generated by RNA polymerase V (Pol V). This targeting recruits DRM2 to deposit de novo methylation in all sequence contexts, particularly at CHH sites. Additionally, a non-canonical RdDM branch involves Pol II-derived siRNAs and AGO6, which also contribute to de novo methylation, especially at specific loci. Thus, MET1, CMT3, and DRM2 are the primary enzymes for CG, CHG, and CHH maintenance, respectively, while 24-nt siRNAs produced via the Pol IV-RDR2-DCL3 pathway are the main guides for RdDM-mediated de novo methylation.

candidates.text: In plants, DNA methylation occurs in three sequence contexts: CG, CHG, and CHH (with H representing A, T, or C), and two key methylation mechanisms are recognized: de novo methylation and maintenance methylation. In Arabidopsis, de novo DNA methylation is mediated by the RNA-directed DNA methylation (RdDM) pathway, while the maintenance of CG, CHG, and CHH methylation is governed by distinct enzymes: DNA methyltransferase 1 (MET1) for CG, chromomethylase 3 (CMT3) for CHG, and both RdDM and chromomethylase 2 (CMT2) for CHH methylation (Matzke and Mosher 2014). In the RdDM pathway, 24-nt siRNAs direct de novo cytosine methylation, with domains rearranged methylase 2 (DRM2) carrying out methylation across all sequence contexts (Matzke and Mosher 2014).
